review_notes: Reviewed all declarations and proofs in the target, with particular attention to the gradient Schwartz encoding and its uses. Also checked related source uses of that encoding; no other concrete simp-interface issue was sufficiently supported.

findings.excerpt:
private theorem weakTestGradientSchwartz_apply
    (ψ : WeakTestFunction (Set.univ : Set Vec3)) (x : L2Vec3) (i : Fin 3) :
    weakTestGradientSchwartz ψ x i =
      (ψ.partialDeriv i (l2Vec3Equiv x) : ℂ) := by
findings.problem: This establishes a useful canonical component normal form for the exposed `weakTestGradientSchwartz` definition, but the theorem is private and is not tagged `[simp]`. Consequently downstream users cannot use this normal form to simplify component expressions; unfolding the definition instead exposes the derivative, postcomposition, and coordinate-equivalence implementation. The file itself uses the equation in a componentwise proof.
findings.proposed_change: Make this equation public and tag it `[simp]`, preserving the stated orientation: `weakTestGradientSchwartz ψ x i` simplifies to `(ψ.partialDeriv i (l2Vec3Equiv x) : ℂ)`.
findings.benefit: Users of the exposed gradient encoding can obtain the coordinate derivative as a stable, concise normal form without unfolding its construction. The rule reduces an application to the mathematical quantity it represents and does not expand that quantity back into the implementation.
